messages:
incident-bot: PAGED via pagerduty -> KV-cache + continuous-batching spike in us-west-2. Multiple hosts showing kvcache size blowups and tail latency regressions. Paging oncall.
alex: oncall here, looking. any customer pages/alerts?
maya: noticing 5% of requests hitting >2s token-latency, error rate up ~0.8% on hosted routes. Dedicated customers seeing throughput cliffs too.
simon: logs show massive KV insert churn after speculative-decoding shots land. looks like draft/target mismatch repeatedly invalidating prefixes.
ryan: +1 saw speculative decoding enabled in canary for rtx-heavy nodes around 09:10 UTC, that aligns.
alex: can we get a short log dump? paste the tail from the runtime.
ops-bot: ```
[09:12:01] kvcache.size=120_000 entries, evict_rate=0
[09:12:02] kvcache.size=240_000 entries, evict_rate=0
[09:12:03] kvcache.size=480_000 entries, evict_rate=0
[09:12:04] continuous_batcher.batch_length=1 -> 44ms
[09:12:05] speculative.decode.mismatch_count=1800
[09:12:06] p99.token_latency=2100ms
```
maya: yikes. evict_rate=0 means no eviction policy hitting. default max_entries maybe bumped by recent config change.
eli: I see a config push at 09:05 that increased kvcache.max_entries to 2_000_000 for the canary pool. that plus speculative decode preferring draft writes could cause runaway growth.
simon: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable speculative decoding on canary pool 2) cap kvcache.max_entries back to safe limit 3) temporarily increase eviction aggressiveness 4) route new traffic to fallback model variant.
alex: agree. can someone run the disable command and cap? i can take routing.
ryan: running disable now.
ryan: `redwoodctl pools update --pool us-west-2-canary --set speculative_decoding=false`
ops-bot: command accepted, rolling update started.
maya: I'll apply kvcache cap change.
maya: `redwoodctl config set runtime.kvcache.max_entries=500000 --scope us-west-2-canary`
ops-bot: config applied to 3/3 hosts.
eli: eviction policy tweak: `runtime.kvcache.eviction_policy=LRU` and `eviction_target=0.7` applied.
ops-bot: eviction policy set, background evictors throttle enabled.
simon: alex can you start diverting traffic off the canary pool to stable?
alex: routing rule update: `routing set-weight model=redwood-ggml-canary us-west-2-canary=0 us-west-2-stable=1` running.
ops-bot: routing update propagated.
alex: monitoring p99 and cache size.
ops-bot: after changes: ```
[09:21:30] kvcache.size=470k -> 210k -> 120k
[09:21:30] evict_rate increased
[09:21:30] speculative.decode.mismatch_count dropping
[09:21:30] p99.token_latency -> 430ms
```
maya: latency trending down. errors decreasing.
ryan: verified dedicated customers on affected pool saw their throughput restored to baseline after routing change.
customer-success: reached out to 2 affected customers (acct A and B). informing them we're rolling mitigations and will follow up with RCA.
alex: good. now we need to coordinate handoff to SRE night shift and collect artifacts for postmortem.
eli: I'll capture config diffs and git commits for the 09:05 change. also saving heap profiles and KV metrics.
simon: note for postmortem: root cause appears to be combined config changes (kvcache cap increased + speculative decoding canary) that interact poorly with continuous batching semantics causing repeated prefix writes and cache divergence.
alex: action items (short):
- eli: upload config diff + heap profiles to incident doc (link)
- maya: prepare rollback timeline + exact commands
- ryan: timeline of requests and launch events
- simon: draft postmortem outline
- customer-success: prepare customer summary
alex: i'm handing off to night oncall @maya for follow-up. please escalate to me if anything regresses.
maya: taking over. will watch for next 2 hours, will start RCA doc now. leaving notes here for next shift:
- don't re-enable speculative decoding on canary until we have regression test for KV divergence
- add kvcache stress test under speculative decoding enabled in CI
- consider adding a TTL on speculative-produced prefixes to limit growth
- consider autoscaling eviction when insertion rate spikes
ops-bot: incident status -> mitigation in place. impact reduced to negligible. creating incident ticket INC-2026-1872.
alex: thanks team. follow-up sync 11:00 UTC to review postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
maya: adding timeline to ticket now. will ping if any customer alarms.
customer-success: we'll share initial note to impacted customers in 30m with high-level mitigation and ETA for RCA.
